Subject: Runtime overlay separation — follow-up and evidence request

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Aurora's security team is documenting vendor separation controls for our upcoming SOC2 scoping. We have two items we still need from Redwood to complete our notebook: a) a simple network diagram that highlights the runtime "overlay" (sidecar/proxy) vs the control plane egress paths, and b) a short threat-model summary that explains how operator access is constrained and what evidence we can expect (audit logs, flow logs, signed attestations).

Specifically: can you confirm whether operator actions ever generate outbound connections to customer VPCs, and whether any control-plane components perform DNS or HTTP egress to third-party domains (packaging repos, telemetry endpoints)? If so, we need justification and a sample of the logs that would show this.

If possible please provide the diagram and a short writeup by EOD Friday — our audit window opens next week.

Appreciate it,
Alice

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. High level answers up front: operator actions do NOT directly open persistent outbound connections into customer VPCs, and control-plane egress is constrained to a small allowlist of telemetry/packaging endpoints (we provide DNS/HTTP allowlist details and signed attestations on request).

I'm attaching a compact diagram that highlights:
- Data plane (inference pods + sidecar proxies) — customer traffic enters, inference executes, KV/cache stays in the pod or encrypted object store.
- Control plane (management API, model registry, scheduling) — runs in Redwood control plane; it performs outbound egress only to explicitly documented endpoints for telemetry and model artifact retrieval.
- Operator demarcation — operator consoles interact with the control plane; operator session proxies are managed in our control plane and are one-way (no operator SSH into customer hosts).

Evidence we can supply:
- Flow log excerpts showing control-plane egress CIDRs and destination domains (egress-proof-log-sample.txt).
- Signed attestations of control-plane container digests and a PDF that maps egress flows to policy (controlplane-demarcation-note.pdf).
- A copy of our runtime-overlay-egress-diagram.png (attached).

Kimberly, Irene — can you add a 2–3 paragraph threat summary about lateral escalation risk if a sidecar were compromised and the mitigations (mutual TLS, short-lived workload certs, KV cache isolation)?

Logan Wright

Hi team — adding the threat-model summary below and two quick implementation notes.

Threat-model summary (short):
- Attack surface: network-facing inference endpoints, sidecar/proxy process, underlying host operator surfaces (operator console/API).
- Key mitigations: per-tenant cryptographic identities (short-lived mTLS certs), network policy enforced at the pod and VPC egress layer, sidecar process sandboxing, and strict key management (KMS-backed keys; no long-lived plaintext keys on disk).
- Lateral escalation scenario: if a sidecar were exploited, an attacker could attempt to (1) intercept or replay requests to other tenants, or (2) exfiltrate cached KV entries. Mitigations reduce these risks by isolating tenant KV namespaces, encrypting cache at rest, and enforcing strict path/host-based allowlists for any outbound flows originating from runtime components.

Implementation notes:
- Operator access: We do not provide operators with direct host-level credentials. Operator actions are calls to the control plane API which itself authenticates and authorizes each action; ephemeral session tokens are audited.
- Egress justification: Control plane retrieves model artifacts from controlled registries and sends anonymous telemetry to a small set of endpoints (listed in the diagram link). For customers with blocked egress we can provide an air-gapped artifact sync flow or ship model bundles.

Attachments provided in this thread: runtime-overlay-egress-diagram.png (annotated), egress-proof-log-sample.txt (flow log extract showing dst domains and ports), controlplane-demarcation-note.pdf (signed by security).

2) For the signed attestations: can you confirm the signing key type and where the public key will be published (we need a verifier for audit).

If you can drop those two items into the Drive link by EOD Monday we'll be able to close the story. Also would prefer a short call (20 minutes) to run through the attestation verification steps with our audit lead. Are you available Monday 10–11am PT?
